subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the wanderer in <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>: a woman with long wavy brown hair, hood down, in a long dark indigo coat with a brown shoulder strap and satchel, holding a tall wooden staff with a hooked top and a small brass lantern.
<Subject 2> is the rendering style of <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>: a hand-drawn night landscape built from thick rhythmic curved strokes and engraved contour lines, a swirling indigo and navy sky with spiraling clouds outlined in pale blue and gold, glowing star orbs ringed with halos, and golden wheat drawn stalk by stalk.
<Subject 3> is the falling star: a bright gold-white point wrapped in spiral halo rings, seen at the upper left of <Picture 1>.
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], showing a low upward view of <Subject 1> from behind, left of centre, her right arm raising the staff so the lantern hangs high, <Subject 3> in the swirling sky at upper left and the huge moon right of centre.
<Picture 2> is the last frame of [Shot 1], showing <Subject 1> from behind her right shoulder, right of centre, facing left toward the moon now on the left side of the frame, holding the lantern up by its handle in her raised left hand while her right hand grips the staff, the lantern blazing white-gold with <Subject 3> inside and rays bursting from it.

detailed_description:
The target video is a hand-drawn night landscape in motion in <Subject 2>: every stroke of the sky, clouds and wheat keeps its drawn texture as it moves, the clouds and star halos slowly swirling.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. <Subject 3> spirals down out of the sky toward her, growing brighter, its halo rings rippling outward through the clouds. She lifts the lantern off the hooked top of the staff with her left hand and holds it up high to meet the star. The star drops into the lantern through its glass, and the lantern flares white-gold, throwing sharp rays across the sky and a pulse of gold light over the wheat, which bends outward in a ring around her. The camera arcs to the right around behind her right shoulder at slow speed in one continuous move, so the huge moon swings from the right side of the frame to the left and she ends facing left toward it. The camera is still arcing as the shot ends on <Picture 2>, the blazing lantern held up in her left hand toward the moon and the staff in her right. No cut or transition occurs.

overall_soundscape:
The crystalline hum rises in pitch as the star falls, then a bright glassy chime rings as it enters the lantern, followed by a soft rushing whoosh as the pulse of light sweeps across the wheat. Wind and crickets continue underneath.
